builder_plan.scenario: You already need task-specific training and want to reduce its memory or compute cost.
builder_plan.change: Change only the training technique on a small controlled run after checking prerequisites.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current training recipe with the same model, data split, and evaluation.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Held-out quality, peak memory, training time, and full compute cost to the target quality.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: POSEIDON: Scaling Training Environments for Scientific Agents from Code Repositories
summary: The pipeline replaces manual construction of agent training environments by automatically extracting, decomposing, and refining executable tasks from scientific code repositories. The cost is a complex multi-stage generation and verification pipeline plus the need to train models on the resulting data, which exceeds a single 24 GB GPU for the reported model sizes. Adoption can fail because environment correctness depends on repository executability and automated verification, and the resulting dataset primarily benefits teams performing model training rather than inference-only deployments.
rationale: The reader lacks the infrastructure to train 9B-35B models and the pipeline targets dataset construction for training, so it is relevant to track but not adoptable in their production practice.
technique: Automated generation of verifiable agent training environments

claims.statement: The pipeline replaces manual construction of agent training environments by automatically extracting, decomposing, and refining executable tasks from scientific code repositories. The cost is a complex multi-stage generation and verification pipeline plus the need to train models on the resulting data, which exceeds a single 24 GB GPU for the reported model sizes. Adoption can fail because environment correctness depends on repository executability and automated verification, and the resulting dataset primarily benefits teams performing model training rather than inference-only deployments.
Models trained on the generated Pearl dataset (97,659 environments) achieve consistent gains across six scientific-agent benchmarks; no single factor is reported.
